title: while Counters
goal: In this lesson you will practice while loops that count up or down with a clear counter pattern.
learn: Count up by adding 1 each pass
Count down until a stop value
Print the counter each time through
idea: A counter is an integer that you change by a fixed amount on each pass, usually +1 or -1. To count up, start at 1, loop while the counter is less than or equal to a limit, print it, then add 1. To count down, start high, loop while it is greater than 0, print it, then subtract 1. Keep the update on its own line so you can see how the loop will end.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change the start of the first loop from n = 1 to n = 3 and press Run. The Up lines should show 3, 4, 5.

practice.text: Count up from 1 to 7 with a while loop. Print each number.
practice.hint: Fill the empty print() with n, then add 1 to n each pass so the loop reaches 7 and stops.
practice.starterTip: Try print(n) in the blank line, then n = n + 1 under the comment. Both indented under while.
practice.starter:
n = 1
while n <= 7:
    print()
    # Add 1 to n
practice.gradingNote: Pass if while prints 1 through 7 and n increases by 1 each time.

practice.text: Count down from 6 to 1. Print each number, then print Blast off! after the loop.
practice.hint: Inside the while, subtract 1 from n after each print. The last print() after the loop is not indented under the while.
practice.starterTip: Add n = n - 1 inside the loop. After while ends, fill print() with print("Blast off!").
practice.gradingNote: Pass if 6 through 1 print, n decreases, then Blast off! (or similar) after the loop.

quiz.question: What does n = n + 1 do in a while loop?

options.text: It moves the counter one step forward

quiz.correct: Right, adding 1 moves the counter toward the stop condition.
quiz.wrong: n = n + 1 increases the counter by one each pass.

quiz.question: If n starts at 1 and the condition is while n <= 3 with n = n + 1, what prints?
quiz.correct: Yes, the loop runs while n is 1, 2, and 3, and then stops.
quiz.wrong: Trace it: print, add 1, check again. It stops when n becomes 4.

quiz.question: Why is a fixed +/- update a good counter pattern?

options.text: It makes infinite loops on purpose
You can predict when the loop will stop

quiz.correct: Right, a steady step makes the stopping point easy to predict.
quiz.wrong: Predictable updates keep while loops finite and safe.
